elements.element: Fallback: licence extends to Customer's affiliates upon written notice
elements.evidence: "IBM grants Customer and, upon written notice to IBM, Customer's Affiliates a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components"

elements.element: Fallback: agreement/licence transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition." (pre-existing, untouched)

elements.element: Preferred: licence extends to Customer's affiliates
elements.evidence: "Customer and, upon written notice to IBM, Customer's Affiliates" (with a notice condition, so preferred-level unconditional coverage is only approximated)

elements.element: Preferred: licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: Grant runs only to "Customer and ... Customer's Affiliates"; no contractor language anywhere.

elements.element: Preferred: paid-up licences perpetual and irrevocable
elements.evidence: Licence remains "nonexclusive, revocable"; no perpetual/irrevocable wording.

elements.element: Preferred: subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: No termination-trigger limitation; the grant is still expressly "revocable".
"Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition."

reasons: Locked fallback level is complete: affiliate coverage on written notice was inserted, and M&A successor transfer already exists in the untouched assignment paragraph, so no second edit was needed.
The edit is a single in-line insertion into the grant sentence; no other sentence, the anti-reverse-engineering covenant, the assignment mechanics, or the no-implied-licence sentence was altered.

Preferred level is not reached (still "revocable", no perpetual/irrevocable paid-up licence, no uncured-material-breach-only termination, no contractor coverage) — correctly not attempted at the locked fallback level, and no preferred-only scope or duration was smuggled in.

Minor drafting note only: "Affiliates" is capitalised but the resolved definitions do not show an Affiliate definition; if the Agreement lacks one, conform to lower case or cross-reference the definition. This does not defeat the fallback.
